input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The guard uses all(...) instead of any(...) over the arguments' help attributes, so the section is gated on every argument being documented rather than on at least one.
- failure path: A command with arguments SRC (help set) and DST (no help) prints no 'Positional arguments' section at all in --help, silently dropping the documented text; conversely a command with zero arguments satisfies all([]) and prints an empty 'Positional arguments' header on every --help.

Reviewer finding
- description: Using all() instead of any() hides the whole positional section when only some arguments have help, even though the docstring says the section is written if at least one argument is documented.
- rationale: Trigger: a command with two arguments, one with help='the source' and one with no help. all() returns False, so the section is skipped and the documented argument disappears from the help output. Before this change, the documented argument was listed. The mechanism contradicts the docstring's stated intent, and the impact is that help text the author wrote is silently dropped.
critique: The finding identifies the same all() vs any() guard error. It describes the same failure path, where a command with one documented and one undocumented argument skips the positional section and drops the documented help. It does not mention the empty-header case for zero arguments, but the core mechanism is the same.
